suggestions.assertion: Quantitative claims in the context carry either a source or a label indicating how they are known
suggestions.reason: The document handles the two contested figures (8s p95, 40% load) with rigorous epistemic labeling, but the third quantitative context fact ('roughly 300 active tenants') carries only the soft qualifier 'roughly' with no explicit source or verification label. A document that labeled 300 tenants the same way could pass this assertion trivially more convincingly; as written, this run passes on the strength of the two headline figures rather than full coverage of every number in context. Consider either scoping the assertion explicitly to 'the two figures the requester flagged as uncertain' or adding a sub-check for the tenant count specifically, so a future run that also leaves the tenant count unlabeled doesn't pass by omission.

eval_feedback.overall: This is an unusually strong, discriminating output: every headline evidentiary assertion is satisfied with substantive, quoted text rather than surface compliance — the document builds an entire 'Evidence and open questions' section and stages the whole design/decision (Phase 0 gating) around not treating unverified numbers as settled facts. The one soft spot is the untagged tenant count, which is a minor and arguably out-of-scope gap given the user themselves did not flag it as uncertain. No assertion here would pass for a clearly bad or generic RFC — each requires the specific evidentiary discipline this run actually demonstrates.
